newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam provinces ignore Hanoi land demand - report.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam provinces ignore Hanoi land demand - report.

text.p: Two thirds of Vietnam's provinces have failed to respond to government demands for detailed information about their land usage, the English-language Vietnam News said on Friday.

The state-controlled daily quoted a report in the Thanh Nien newspaper and a speech to the National Assembly by Agriculture Minister Nguyen Cong Tan as saying the lack of information meant the central government was unable to complete land-use plans.
Land use rights and ownership are a highly sensitive and occasionally emotional issue in communist Vietnam.
Values have shot up since economic reforms were introduced in the late 1980s, and exchanges of land are reported to be often associated with corruption.
All land is owned by the state, but efforts by authorities to reclaim plots have occasionally resulted in demonstrations or violence.
The Vietnam News report said that in the two years since Hanoi launched its survey, only 18 of Vietnam's 53 cities and provinces had responded in detail.
Just 15 districts out of 673 and 3,000 out of 10,031 villages were actively working to complete the land usage plans, it added.

A woman died earlier this year during a bloody clash between some 1,000 villagers and around 500 riot police over moves by authorities to evict them from a paddy field being reclaimed for a luxury golf-course on the outskirts of Hanoi.
Around 80 percent of Vietnam's 75 million population live in rural areas.
